Let $\angle XOA = \theta$ is an acute angle. From the adjacent figure, according to the definition

$$\sin \theta = \frac{PM}{OP}, \text{cosec } \theta = \frac{1}{\sin \theta} = \frac{OP}{PM}$$

$$\cos \theta = \frac{OM}{OP}, \sec \theta = \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \frac{OP}{OM}$$

$$\tan \theta = \frac{PM}{OM}, \cot \theta = \frac{1}{\tan \theta} = \frac{OM}{PM}$$

Again, $\tan \theta = \frac{PM}{OM} = \frac{\frac{PM}{OP}}{\frac{OM}{OP}}$ [dividing the numerator and the denominator by $OP$]

Or, $\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}$

$$\therefore \tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}$$

and similarly,

$$\cot \theta = \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}$$

figures.caption: Fig 9.01: Trigonometric ratios in a right-angled triangle
figures.description: A right-angled triangle OMP with angle theta at O, where PM is the opposite side, OM is the adjacent side, and OP is the hypotenuse.
